takeaway: Most cervical cancers are HPV-associated; squamous cell carcinoma is 70–80%. Assess PD-L1 by combined positive score when it would change treatment, and submit all lymph-node tissue in 2 mm sections [1].
clinicalQuestion: How does the ESMO cervical-cancer guideline frame cause, histology, and key pathology or biomarker steps?
background: ESMO published an updated clinical practice guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up [1].
studyDesign: ESMO clinical practice guideline with graded recommendations.
intervention: HPV-aware diagnosis, PD-L1 testing when actionable, and complete lymph-node submission.
primaryOutcome: Diagnostic and staging recommendations that direct treatment.
mainFindings: The vast majority of cervical carcinomas are HPV-associated, whereas 10–15% are HPV-independent. Squamous-cell carcinoma accounts for 70–80% and adenocarcinoma for 20–25%. Total submission of the lymph node in 2 mm sections is recommended [III, A]. Assessing PD-L1 by combined positive score is recommended when it has therapeutic implications [I, A]. In locally advanced disease, PET-CT sensitivity for pelvic nodes is 0.88 (95% CI 0.40–0.99) and specificity 0.93 (0.85–0.97); for para-aortic nodes sensitivity is 0.40 (0.18–0.66) and specificity 0.93 (0.91–0.95) [1].
clinicalMeaning: Do not assume every cervical cancer is HPV-positive, and do not skip PD-L1 when the result would change systemic therapy [1].
limitations: Only recommendations that were fully readable in the extracted text are used. Drug regimens are not invented from headings [1].
bottomLine: Record HPV status and histology, submit nodes at 2 mm, and order PD-L1 CPS when it will change treatment [1].
practiceImplication: Use PET-CT knowing pelvic-node sensitivity is high but imprecise, and para-aortic sensitivity is only 0.40 [1].
trustRationale: Current ESMO guideline with explicit evidence levels.
whatNotToOverclaim: A self-sampling HPV screening paper is not the treatment guideline.
